#2747. As Chargers' offense struggles, Mike McDaniel will move from the sideline to the booth

Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will get a different perspective on his struggling offense on Sunday against the Texans.

McDaniel said today that he will move upstairs to the booth to call plays after previously working from the sideline.

“One of the things that I want to try is call plays from the box to see adjustments for myself and communicate with the position coaches appropriately what things we can focus on between series,” McDaniel said. “I won’t be in the same spot.”

Although the Chargers’ offense has been among the worst in the NFL this season and head coach Jim Harbaugh has faced questions about whether he should fire his offensive coordinator, McDaniel insisted that he’s not concerned about the criticism.

“My problem solving doesn’t come from insecurity,” McDaniel said. “I’m not trying to prove or justify anything.”

The Chargers rank dead last in the NFL in scoring, having scored only 99 points this season, and they have an NFL-high 17 turnovers. McDaniel said he thinks it’s worth trying something different while delegating some of what he had been doing on the sideline to the assistant coaches.

“Seems like a good action to take based on how things have gone this year, and realistically something that I’ve only brought up because I’ve observed, I’m very confident in the rest of the offensive coaching staff and how they’re able to set the tone and communicate information on the sidelines. So I feel a little more comfortable to try that,” McDaniel said.

If that doesn’t work, Harbaugh’s next step might be to move McDaniel from the booth to the unemployment line.

#2745. NFL Injury Report, Week 9: Latest news, updates on Mike Evans, Garrett Wilson, more players for fantasy football

Week 9 is the official midway point of the 2026 NFL season. So by now you know what you have on your fantasy football roster. You also know who has been healthy the majority of the year and which players have missed time. The injuries keep coming as we get into the middle of the campaign. As always, we're tracking all the latest news and updates for you, to help with those fantasy football lineups.

Lamar Jackson, BAL (thumb) — Will be placed on injured reserve

Tyler Huntley, BAL (toe) — Reportedly done for the season

Kyler Murray, MIN (hamstring) — Ruled out for MNF

Deshaun Watson, CLE (concussion protocol)

Murray: The Vikings are going to hold out Murray from MNF against the Bills in Week 9 and Carson Wentz will take over as the starting QB. It's somewhat of a "soft" benching for Murray, who had been struggling to get the passing game going during his starts. With Wentz in the fold, it's an upgrade to the passing game — not by much, but enough. Justin Jefferson should get a nice boost given their history together, while Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson get elevated a bit as well.

Ravens QBs: Jackson left in the first half of Sunday's loss to the Bills. He needs surgery on his thumb and is headed for IR. He'll miss at least four games, if not the rest of the season. After Jackson exited, Huntley entered the game and also had to leave due to injury (turf toe), which will end his season. That leaves Baltimore down to third-string rookie Joe Fagnano, who will start against Jacksonville on TNF. Hayden Winks takes a closer look at what Fagnano could bring. The Ravens traded for Jacoby Brissett, but he will not be ready to play this week.

The QB instability is obviously a huge downgrade to the passing game. Fagnano went 10 of 21 for 91 yards and an INT in his first NFL action in Week 8. Zay Flowers is more of a WR3/flex option while Derrick Henry should get a healthy amount of work, though in a tough matchup. Outside of those two, the rest of the Ravens offense should be avoided in fantasy until we see more from Fagnano or the Ravens make a deal for a QB.

Darnold: The Seahawks will be without Darnold in Week 9 against the Cardinals due to quad and rib injuries. With Darnold out, the Seahawks plan to start Drew Lock … who is also dealing with an elbow injury. Lock was excellent when he had to start in place of Darnold against Arizona in Week 2, going 19 of 26 for 235 yards and three touchdowns in a 31-7 win. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 155 yards and three touchdowns in that game, proving JSN is QB-proof and an auto-start again this week.

Bhayshul Tuten, JAX (ankle/foot) — Should be good to play

Jeremiyah Love, ARI (ankle) — Will be placed on IR, miss 4-5 weeks

Breece Hall, NYJ (quad) — Expected to be back in Week 9

Travis Etienne Jr., NO (hamstring) — Could be activated off IR

Tuten: Jeremy Fowler is reporting that Tuten "should be" good to go for TNF against Baltimore barring any setbacks. Tuten was a DNP all three days to start the week, with ankle and foot issues. He is coming off his best game of the season. He took 18 touches for 159 yards and two scores in Week 8. Chris Rodriguez Jr. is also dealing with a hand injury but was limited on Monday and Tuesday. With Tuten looking like he'll play, he's a solid RB2/3 in most formats. C-Rod isn't really a viable option but could get some carries given Tuten went into this game banged up. Rodriguez is a risky flex play at best.

Hall: We thought the Jets were going to get back Hall in Week 8 against the Raiders. That wasn't the case and we got another solid game from Braelon Allen. At this point, even if Hall comes back, expect Allen to be involved given how well he's performed. Allen is the RB5 overall in half-PPR scoring from Weeks 5-8 with Hall sidelined. We'll need to get a look at how the split is in Week 9 with Hall back, who told Rich Cimini that he is "good to go" for Week 9. Plus, it's a tough draw against Kansas City's run defense. But better matchups loom, so don't be surprised if both Hall and Allen are viable RB2/3 options.

Cardinals RBs: Love suffered a new high-ankle sprain in the comeback win over Dallas in OT on Sunday. Knight exited after a big hit and should land in concussion protocol. It'll be tough for Knight to clear in time for Week 9 against the Seahawks, but we'll see. Love has had so many issues with the ankle in his rookie season, and is expected to miss 4-5 weeks while on injured reserve, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. With Love already out, if Knight sits, Tyler Allgeier will be playable, but don't expect 33.6 fantasy points — or anywhere close to that — against Seattle's top defense.

But with Love on IR and Knight starting the season with a lesser role, expect Allgeier to be the lead back moving forward. There could be weeks when Knight is healthy in which the staff rides the hot hand. But Allgeier was brought in to be a high-value backup to Love. Allgeier will have RB2/3 value week-to-week depending on the matchup. Also keep an eye out for James Conner, who is on IR but could be a useful stash.

McCaffrey: CMC comes off the bye navigating a mild hamstring strain. It doesn't feel like this will cause him to miss Week 9 against the Raiders. But we saw before San Francisco's bye that Kyle Shanahan feels comfortable giving the ball to rookie Kaelon Black. We could see more of Black on Sunday to help keep McCaffrey fresh.

Mike Evans, SF (Achilles) — Unlikely to play

Garrett Wilson, NYJ (concussion protocol)

Emeka Egbuka, TB (foot) — Could play in Week 9

Jordyn Tyson, NO (hamstring) — Could come off IR

Deebo Samuel Sr., SF (hamstring) — Unlikely to play

G. Wilson: The Jets' receiver missed another practice on Thursday and it's looking unlikely he'll clear concussion protocol in time to play Sunday against the Chiefs. If that's the case, Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. would benefit with more targets. We all know what happened last week but QB Geno Smith would be forced to spread it around a bit more. TE Mason Taylor is also banged up, so if both Wilson and Taylor are out, Kenyon Sadiq would get a bump as well. It's a tough matchup against the K.C. secondary, but the game script should favor the Jets throwing the ball plenty.

49ers WRs: Niners GM John Lynch told reporters on Thursday that Evans and Samuel are unlikely to return for Week 9's matchup against the Raiders. But Demarcus Robinson and KhaDarel Hodge are expected to be back. The expectation was for Evans and Samuel to potentially be back after the Week 8 bye. That doesn't seem to be the case, so San Fran will be thin at WR again. Robinson's return is interesting, though we don't know what to expect from him coming off injury. It was a mixed bag of receivers in Week 7 with Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, Jacob Cowing and Christian Kirk splitting snaps. George Kittle will remain the primary target for QB Brock Purdy until Evans is back.

Watson: The Packers' lead receiver had a miraculous exit and return to TNF's win over the Panthers in Week 8. Watson finished with an 8-113-0 line on 10 targets, catching a few passes after coming back from the hospital. But Watson revealed he's dealing with a broken rib, which is less than ideal. He'll have ample time to rest before Week 9's matchup with the Patriots. Watson could play through the injury, but if he's active, he would be at risk of exiting the game early. If Watson ends up having to sit, Tucker Kraft and Savion Williams would likely see more targets. Matthew Golden would be elevated into WR1 territory as well.

M. Wilson: The Cardinals' receiver told reporters after Sunday's win over the Cowboys that he's dealing with broken ribs. It appears Wilson is going to play through the injury. He's a risky option in the flex in PPR formats going up against the Seahawks' stout defense in Week 9.

Egbuka: The Bucs wideout has missed the past two games, and Tampa's passing game sure could use him. The Bucs didn't complete a pass in Week 8's shutout win over the Falcons, instead opting to run the ball 56 times for 324 yards. That likely won't be the case in Chicago in Week 9. If Egbuka can get back — he practiced in full Thursday — it's a decent matchup, though Tampa Bay ranks dead last in passing offense this season. Egbuka would be a risky flex at best.

Henry: The Patriots listed Henry as DNP again at practice Thursday. That puts his status for Week 9 against the Packers in doubt. If Henry were to sit, Eli Raridon would see the majority of the snaps and targets at tight end. The rookie out of Notre Dame has already proven to be a commodity in the passing game with a pair of TDs this season. He'd be a high-end TE2 with TE1 upside this week if Henry sits.

Ferguson: The Cowboys lost Ferguson to a low-ankle sprain early in the game against Arizona. He didn't return and his status for Week 9 against the Colts could be up in the air. If Ferguson is out, this is still a passing game dominated by CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Ryan Flournoy has stepped up as a solid WR3 as well. Brevyn Spann-Ford played 88% of the snaps in Week 8 and had four catches on five targets for 31 yards. In deeper formats, Spann-Ford isn't a bad streamer. He could see garbage-time looks if the Cowboys run away against a struggling Indy team.

#2744. Bronny James headed to G League after dismal start to Lakers season

Bronny James is headed east to California's Coachella Valley, as the Lakers have assigned the third-year player to its G League affiliate.

The team announced the move Thursday, and the 22-year-old, along with teammate Cameron Carr, will suit up for the Coachella Valley Lakers, which begin their season on Friday. This follows the Los Angeles Lakers' 116-103 win over the Sacramento Kings on Wednesday.

James barely factored into the game, logging a single minute. Early on, he hasn't been able to crack regular minutes this season.

Through nine games, James has had cameos in five contests with averages of 2.4 minutes and 0.8 points per game. His most recent productive effort came against the Heat when he chipped in two points and a block in a single minute of play.

Lakers news: Is this the best version of Lakers star Luka Dončić we've ever seen?

Bronny James has seen his minutes decrease drastically from the previous season, wherein he logged 6.7 minutes per game over 27 games in his rookie campaign and 8.9 minutes per game over 42 games the following season, 2025-2026.

James' father, legendary NBA star LeBron James, is no longer with the Lakers. The 41-year-old is playing for the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year deal with a player option.

For the Lakers, the early returns for the roster have been positive. The team is 7-2 and is atop the Pacific Division thanks to inspired play from star Luka Dončić. With eight players averaging 23 minutes or more per game, it's clear James has less opportunity to crack the rotation.

The Coachella Valley Lakers open play at Acrisure Arena on Friday, Nov. 6 vs. the Salt Lake City Stars. Whether the game is a precursor to a brief stint or a more prolonged development period remains to be seen.

#2743. Clemson freshman QB pokes fun at Florida State’s empty stadium before Syracuse game

Noise in the Clemson Tigers' media center forced quarterback Tait Reynolds to wait during his press conference on Wednesday, Nick Kosko noted for On3, and the interruption sent the freshman's mind back to Saturday's trip to Tallahassee.

"I think Florida State was playing some crowd noise. It got louder throughout the game. There was nobody there. It got loud. I was like, 'What the heck?'" Reynolds said with a smile.

Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney during the first half at the annnual Clemson Orange and White spring game at Memorial Stadium in Clemson, South Carolina Saturday, March 28, 2026.

Reynolds was joking, and the joke landed because of how the last week has gone for the Florida State Seminoles.

Before Clemson's 36-24 win on Oct. 31, a plane circled Doak Campbell Stadium towing a banner that called for the firing of head coach Mike Norvell and the removal of board chairman Peter Collins, with Norvell's name misspelled. Dabo Swinney brought it up afterward, on behalf of the opposing coach.

"It was embarrassing what I saw above the stadium. Whoever did that, man, you ought to be ashamed of yourself. And they didn't even spell his name right," Swinney said.

Florida State played the fourth quarter in front of a mostly empty stadium and fired Norvell the next day, ending a seven-year run at 41-39. Rick Stockstill is now the interim coach of a 3-5 team.

A less scandalous explanation than a sound system sits in the box score: Florida State trailed 29-10 with under nine minutes to play, then scored 14 straight points to make it 29-24. Whoever had stayed finally had something to yell about. Reynolds ended it on third-and-12 with 3:17 left, running 79 yards for a touchdown, the longest run ever by a Clemson quarterback.

Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney during Tiger Walk before the annnual Clemson Orange and White spring game at Memorial Stadium in Clemson, South Carolina Saturday, March 28, 2026.

Clemson entered the game with two touchdown passes all season, the fewest in FBS, and had gone four games without one, its longest drought since 2005. Reynolds threw two against Florida State, finishing 18 of 32 for 189 yards, and added 85 rushing yards on 14 carries.That was quite a night for a quarterback who in September became the earliest freshman to start for Clemson in more than 50 years, and it helps explain the mood on Wednesday.

The win moved Clemson to 5-3 and 3-2 in the ACC, one victory from bowl eligibility. The next stop is the indoor JMA Wireless Dome, where the Tigers face the Syracuse Orange at noon ET on Saturday on ESPN2.

#2737. 2026-27 NHL season predictions: Expert picks for Stanley Cup playoffs, champion and major awards this season

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Following a brief offseason and an expedited preseason, the 2026-27 NHL season has arrived. Before the puck drops on opening night, we have some predictions to make.

If this season feel like it's staring earlier than usual, that's because it is. The NHL is adopting an 84-game regular season, which just means more hockey for the rest of us. That also means a long and arduous journey to the Stanley Cup is ever so slightly more difficult.

So, what will that journey look like? The Carolina Hurricanes are looking to defend their title as Cup champions, but they'll have to contend with a deep Eastern Conference and some real juggernauts in the Western Conference. With that in mind, we logged our expert predictions for the playoff field in each conference -- and there were a few surprises -- before making our Stanley Cup Final selections.

We also called our shot on the winners of each major individual award. Connor McDavid is looking for his fourth Hart Trophy, but he's got some competition from an up-and-coming superstar in his own division. Races for the Norris Trophy and Vezina Trophy should be pretty wide open, and unexpected candidates always emerge throughout the season.

It should be a fun season in the NHL, so follow along with all our coverage at CBS Sports. Let's get things kicked off with the season preview and predictions, which will of course be 100% accurate.

Baumgartner: I don't see many new faces entering the conversation when it comes to the Eastern Conference playoff race. A healthy Florida Panthers side will slot themselves right back towards the top of the Atlantic, and a revamped Washington Capitals side should be able to make some noise in the Metropolitan. Besides that, I have six 2026 playoff teams returning to the dance in 2027.

Nivison: As much as I hate to go with chalk in preseason predictions -- because it rarely happens that way -- there's no denying the top dogs in the West. The Avalanche and Stars are the class of the Central Division, and the Golden Knights should pound a pitiful Pacific Division into a pulp. Things get more interesting behind those clear Cup contenders, and I'm projecting another significant leap forward from the Mammoth. I also think Macklin Celebrini will be successful in dragging the Sharks to the playoffs in his third NHL season.

Nivison -- Columbus Blue Jackets: The Blue Jackets have been agonizingly close to the playoffs in each of the last two seasons, and I think they get over the hump in 2026-27. There are still questions in Columbus. Can Adam Fantilli be a franchise player at center? Is the forward group as a whole good enough to keep pace in a competitive Eastern Conference? Still, I am sure the Blue Jackets have a really strong blue line, led by Norris Trophy winner Zach Werenski, and goaltender Jet Greaves is on track to become a Vezina Trophy candidate. Internal improvements from the young core will then get Columbus above the cut line.

Baumgartner -- San Jose Sharks: The Sharks narrowly missed out on the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, finishing just four points short of the second wild card. San Jose added a good group of veterans over the summer, but the most important offseason move was selecting Ivar Stenberg with the No. 2 pick in the Draft. Stenberg joins the youth movement in San Jose, which is spearheaded by new captain Macklin Celebrini, who broke the Sharks single-season points record with 115 last season. The Sharks are a better team than they were last year, and with Celebrini entering his third season as a legit Hart Trophy contender, this team won't be fun to play against.

Nivison: Yes, the Mammoth have a brutal path coming out of the Central Divison, but just close your eyes and imagine this scenario with me. Logan Cooley becomes a superstar center. Dylan Guenther hits 50 goals. Dmitry Simashev asserts himself as a budding top-four defenseman. Anders Lee and Vincent Trocheck provide necessary veteran depth. Now open your eyes. Utah is your Western Conference champion.

Unfortunately for the Mammoth, they will run into a refreshed Panthers team that now has double-barreled Tkachuks. Last season, we found out that all it takes to stop Florida is to hope all of its key players miss significant time with injury. The long offseason was probably a blessing in disguise as it allowed the Panthers to get healthy, and that's bad news for everyone else. The structure in front of the crease will limit some of the volatility we saw from Jacob Markstrom in New Jersey, and Florida wins its third Stanley Cup in four years.

Baumgartner: Before last season, the Carolina Hurricanes' kryptonite was the Eastern Conference Final. The Hurricanes were able to overcome their demons and win the East before ultimately taking home the franchise's first Stanley Cup since 2006. In the West, the Dallas Stars have been running into the same problem. After three straight seasons ending in the Western Conference Final, the Stars regressed last postseason, flaming out in the first-round to the Minnesota Wild. The Central Division will once again be a gauntlet, but I'm ready for Dallas to take the next step and reach the Stanley Cup Final.

While Dallas has continued to fall short in recent years, the Panthers have done the opposite. The Panthers made three consecutive Stanley Cup Final appearances, winning back-to-back Cups in 2023-24 and 2024-25. Last season, Florida's three-peat attempt came to a halt on day one of training after captain Aleksander Barkov went down with a non-contact injury, tearing both the ACL and MCL in his right knee. An offseason of healing for Barkov, and the rest of the banged up Panthers, has the team refreshed entering September for the first time in years. With nearly the entire 2025 Stanley Cup winning core still on the team and Brady Tkachuk added to the fold, Florida looks ready to win its third Stanley Cup in four seasons.

Nivison: Celebrini should have won the Hart Trophy last season, but for some incomprehensible reason, he wasn't even a finalist. This year, Celebrini replicates that performance and gets San Jose to the postseason to take home his first MVP award at age 20. Hughes posts a career year in his first full season with the Wild, and Spencer Carberry gets his flowers for winning the Metro Division after missing the playoffs last year.

Baumgartner: McDavid's ability to take over a game was evident nearly every time he touched the ice last season. His 24 points (11 goals,13 assists) in the final 14 games of the regular season -- without Leon Draisaitl in the lineup -- was one of the many reasons I put him No. 1 on my Hart Trophy ballot. With just two years left on his current contract, desperation may start to kick in to get the job in Edmonton, which would lead to another MVP-caliber season. Barkov is healthy and the frontrunner to win his fourth Selke, and Dahlin will have another strong season to take home his first career Norris Trophy.

#2733. Bronny James assigned to G League's Coachella Valley Lakers after playing limited minutes early in third NBA season

Bronny James made the Los Angeles Lakers' 2026-27 opening night roster, securing a spot while his draft classmate, first-round pick Dalton Knecht, was waived.

But after James averaged 2.4 minutes in five appearances amid the Lakers' 7-2 start, the team announced Thursday that it assigned the 2024 second-round pick to the G League's Coachella Valley Lakers.

Fellow guard Cameron Carr was also sent to the franchise's G League affiliate ahead of its Friday night season opener against the Utah Jazz's Salt Lake City Stars.

Bronny James — in his first season in the Lakers' organization without his father, LeBron James — previously spent time in the G League, where his stat lines have often dwarfed those he has authored in the NBA.

Across a combined 25 regular-season games the past two seasons with the then-South Bay Lakers — who have since relocated and rebranded — Bronny James posted 18.4 points, 4.4 assists, 4 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game while shooting 49.6% from the field, including 41.3% from beyond the arc.

James, now 22, was the No. 55 pick when he was drafted out of USC more than two years ago. He appeared in 27 regular-season games with the Lakers as a rookie, making father-son history but struggling mightily at times, particularly early on.

He made noticeable progress in Year 2, taking the court for 42 regular-season games and raising his field-goal percentage from 31.3% (2024-25) to 40.9% (2025-26) and his 3-point percentage from 28.1% (2024-25) to 38.6% (2025-26).

Head coach JJ Redick saw enough from James to include him in his playoff rotation last season, albeit a shorthanded one.

That paved the way for additional excitement and milestones.

Coming into Year 3, the question was: How would James fare without his superstar father on the Lakers (including how would he be treated by staff and teammates in the absence of the future Hall of Famer)?

But James hasn't been given much of an opportunity in the regular season to make any kind of jump. In his sparing minutes, he scored 0.8 points per game. He attempted only three field goals and made two of them.

James could wind up back with the Lakers soon, but his lack of on-court involvement so far isn't promising, in terms of his chances of carving out the long-term 3-and-D role he teased on occasion last season.

As for Knecht, he ended up signing a two-way deal with the New York Knicks, for whom he logged 10 points on 4-of-6 shooting, plus seven rebounds, on Wednesday in a win over the Chicago Bulls.

Patriots owner Robert Kraft recently underwent back surgery, which will keep him sidelined on "injured reserve" and force him to miss Rob Gronkowski's induction into the Patriots Hall of Fame on Saturday.

"As much pain as I was in before having surgery, it pains me even more to miss the ceremony," Kraft, 85, told Mike Reiss of ESPN on Thursday.

#2728. Chiefs receiver Rice files for bankruptcy amid lawsuits

Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice has filed for bankruptcy in Texas, citing civil lawsuit settlements stemming from a 2024 car crash among his $3.45 million in debts.

The court filing submitted on Wednesday in the US Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Texas lists $677,054 in total personal property assets.

That includes Rice's Super Bowl ring from the Chiefs' victory over the San Francisco 49ers in the NFL's title game in February 2024, which according to the documents Rice used as collateral with Thomas McMurray, the lawyer representing him in pending civil litigations.

Rice was suspended for the first six games of the 2025 NFL season over his involvement in the 2024 high-speed crash in which his Lamborghini SUV was clocked at 119 mph (191.51 km/h) on a Dallas highway.

An ensuing multi-car crash left several injured and Rice fled on foot.

He apologized in a statement before turning himself in to authorities. Rice pleaded guilty to felony charges in the crash and was sentenced to five years of probation and 30 days' jail time.

The court documents filed Wednesday show Rice has been paying crash victim Kathryn Kuykendall through garnishment of his Chiefs paychecks, with $979,837 still owed.

The documents list as "disputed" a claim of $200,000 to former girlfriend Dacoda Jones, who in February accused him of assaulting her and launched a civil suit against him.

Three other claims amounting to $650,000 to three other crash victims are listed as "disputed".

Other debts include unsecured bank loans.

The 26-year-old Rice is in the final year of his rookie contract and is expected to make $1,560,711 in base salary in 2026.

Rice, who returned to action on Sunday after missing two games with a hamstring injury, has played in five games this season with 20 catches and two touchdowns.

#2726. Three reasons why the Brewers can repeat as World Series champions in 2027

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Milwaukee Brewers are the freshly crowned World Series champions for 2026. Add that trophy to a regular season body of work in which they won 103 games and achieved the best run differential in all of Major League Baseball, and it's clear the Brewers this season did all a team can do. The first title in franchise history will be remembered and cherished by the Brewers and their fans forever, and it was earned in every respect.

The celebrations won't soon end, and the post-Game 5 hangovers are still pulsing. Even so, it's time to turn our attention to the 2027 season and explore why the Brewers absolutely have the foundation necessary to do it all again next year. Here, then, are three reasons the Brewers can become repeat champions roughly one year from now.

Eyeball the Brewers' current contract obligations and service time tiers, and you'll find just six players are likely bound for free agency. Brandon Woodruff, Jake Bauers, JoJo Romero, and Gary Sánchez will be free agents soon. Elsewhere, Dustin May has a mutual option for 2027, which means he'll probably join them. Finally, Antonio Senzatela has a $14 million team option for 2027 on which the Brewers may pass.

Of those, the 31-year-old Bauers is the biggest needle-mover, as he's coming off a 2026 season in which he hit 26 home runs in 144 games and put up a WAR of 3.3. He does seem likely to move on, but the Brewers are more than resourceful enough to find comparable production from the non-premium position of first base.

Elsewhere, the Brewers should resist the temptation to trade away catcher, linchpin, and reigning World Series MVP William Contreras ahead of his walk year in 2027. The Brewers Way in recent years has been to part ways with core contributors around such a time, and that may be a temptation with Contreras, especially given Bo Naylor's presence on the roster. Contreras, though, is not easily replaceable given his skills behind the mask and his high level of production at the plate. An extension may not be something the Brewers will pursue – even though the ongoing CBA negotiations will probably lead to a new system that benefits teams like Milwaukee – but even if that's the case, they should keep their catcher and leader around for the final year of team control in the name of defending the belt and the title.

The champion Brewers, as a club that gets limited investment from ownership and is elite at player development, skews young even as they stand as the best team in baseball. Consider:

As for specific examples, they're not hard to find. Budding star Jackson Chourio will be in his age-23 campaign in 2027. Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson will each be 25. Cooper Pratt, like Chourio, will be 23. The Brewers this past season got 16.4 WAR from those names, and Pratt and Henderson didn't even log full seasons.

Let's also note that Brice Turang, who led the Brewers this season with a WAR of 7.3, will be just 27 in '27 and thus should continue performing at a high level. This isn't just a matter of the Brewers being largely shielded from age-related decline next season. There's also the distinct possibility that so many of their 2026 pace-setters are still pre-prime and may have even better days ahead.

As though all of the above weren't enough, the Brewers right now have managed to thread this rare needle: they're the best team at the highest level and have one of the best collections of talent down on the farm. MLB.com in August ranked the Brewers as the third-best farm system in the game right now. FanGraphs ranked them third based on average prospect value. Baseball America at midseason likewise ranked the Milwaukee system third and after the season gave the system an "A" grade.

At an individual level, a number of premium Brewers prospects figure to arrive at some point next season. That list includes shortstop Jesús Made, who may be the top prospect in the game right now. Other 2027 arrivals may include talents like corner infielder Andrew Fischer, right-handers Tyson Hardin and Bishop Letson, and infielder/outfielder Jett Williams, among others. So many teams in contending mode have a fairly dry pipeline thanks to the low draft picks and the now-for-later trades that often accompany World Series aspirations, but that's very much not the case with lead executive Matt Arnold and the Brewers.

Celebrations of the work done in 2026 should be the focus right now for the Crew and their rooters, and once that dies down, they can all be further buoyed by the reality that the Brewers aren't going anywhere. The guess here is that the Brewers open the 2027 season – whatever it looks like — as the consensus favorites to do it all again.

#2725. Cleveland Browns are still struggling to change the team’s culture

The Cleveland Browns have long been the league's little brother that other teams like to bully, especially in the AFC North.

There have been times over the years when a player has tried to insert that missing level of fight back, with former quarterback Baker Mayfield coming to mind.

Even though Mayfield is five years and three teams removed from the Browns, he has not lost any of his feistiness, which was on full display during Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.

While attempting to block down the field on Kenny Gainwell's fourth-quarter touchdown run, Mayfield was dumped into a mud puddle by Atlanta safety Jessie Bates III. Mayfield popped back up, but more importantly, one of his offensive linemen quickly came to his defense and got after Bates.

Now contrast that with two plays from Sunday as the Browns were once again bullied by the Steelers.

On the game's opening possession, quarterback Deshaun Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit from Pittsburgh safety Jaquan Brisker that left Watson lying face down on the field. While he was able to return to the game, Watson suffered a concussion that will likely sideline him for this week's game against the New Orleans Saints.

Later in the game, defensive end Jared Verse was dangerously dropped on his head by Pittsburgh offensive lineman Mason McCormick during an extra-point attempt. Verse was fortunate that he was not injured in what was clearly a dirty play.

Brisker and McCormick were both penalized for the plays, but did anyone on the Browns stick up for Watson or Verse? Did a lineman let Brisker know that the quarterback is off limits? Or call out McCormick?

If you have watched the Browns for any time, you know the answer to those questions.

Watson has not commented on the hit as he is busy recovering in the league-mandated concussion protocol. But on Thursday, Verse let it be known that he was not happy that no one stepped up when he went down, according to Mary Kay Cabot at cleveland.com:

"The lack of reaction by those around me upset me a lot. Not any aspect of anybody; we're focused on the game and everything like that. But a similar play happened to Derek Barnett; I think the next field goal and I spazzed. I lost it because it was my brother and my teammate. When you do something like that, it really upsets me very deeply.

"So, I could tell that from that point on, I was like, we have to do better. We have to get better on every aspect of the game of being mentally aware of, these are my brothers and we're not fighting for each other. We're just kind of focused on the one aspect of the game."

Several of Verse's teammates, including linebackers Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams, said they did not see the play, while Barnett said he would have defended Verse if he had seen the play, but cautioned that the Browns can't let a situation like that get out of hand.

No one is looking for the Browns to turn into the Oakland Raiders of the 1970s, although they were the only team that stood up to the Steelers, so maybe a little bit of that attitude would be nice.

Winning, of course, is the best revenge. But if the Browns are truly committed to changing the culture of the team, which is something that Verse has been vocal about since arriving in town from the Los Angeles Rams, then standing up for a fallen teammate from time to time would not be such a bad idea.

#2723. Deniz Undav plays down Germany call-up hopes amid goal drought

VfB Stuttgart forward Deniz Undav is not expecting to be called up for Germany's upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures.

The 30-year-old was asked whether he was hoping for a call-up in the mixed zone after Stuttgart's 2-0 defeat to Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

“Not at all. Without goals, it's difficult to get into the squad,” he replied, adding that he had yet to receive any indication that he could be selected.

Undav has found the net just twice in 14 appearances in all competitions this season and is still waiting for his first Bundesliga goal of the 2026/27 campaign.

“I have no comment on why there have been so few goals. I genuinely don't know. I'm trying to work on it, but it's just not happening. Somehow, I can't seem to get going,” Undav said.

Having left Undav out of his first squad, Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp is set to announce his second selection on Thursday.

#2722. NFL trade deadline: 3 teams that could deal for Saints DB Justin Reid

Which New Orleans Saints players could be on the move at the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline? The latest reporting has highlighted names like right guard Cesar Ruiz, linebacker Pete Werner, and running back Kendre Miller, but another one to watch is veteran safety Justin Reid. With no guarantees left on his contract in 2027 and a dearth of quality safety play around the league, he could have some appeal to teams in the playoff hunt. Reid doesn't generate many turnovers but he's a reliable tackler with meaningful postseason experience.

Sure, trading Reid wouldn't help the Saints' salary cap situation (saving about $650,000 this year and nearly breaking even in 2027). But trading the 29-year old would open up snaps for younger players with something to prove like Jordan Howden, who will be a free agent in the spring. Special teams aces Lorenzo Styles Jr. and Mike Reid could also compete for more snaps. It's important the Saints find out what they have in these guys on the bottom of the depth chart and determine if any of them can handle a larger role, or at least be part of the plan moving forwards. If the Saints can get another at-bat in the 2027 NFL Draft or improve the picks they already have, even better.

With that in mind, here are three trade proposals we'd hear out before next week's deadline.

New Orleans gets: 2027 sixth-round pick (No. 185)

Buffalo could use another safety after cutting former Saints draft pick C.J. Gardner-Johnson, who ranked third on the team in snaps played (394) and first missed tackles (9). Cole Bishop is an every-down starter at the other safety spot, but the Bills lack a proven commodity next to him. Damar Hamlin is a good backup but he only has two years of starting experience. Reid is someone Buffalo could lean on.

Jacksonville gets: S Justin Reid, 2028 seventh-round pick (TBD)

New Orleans gets: 2027 fifth-round pick (No. 164)

Antonio Johnson has played really well when healthy (so much so that we targeted him in our bye week 2027 mock offseason), and he's set to return from an ankle injury on Thursday Night Football. But the Jaguars have struggled to get consistency out of the other safety spot between Eric Murray and Rayuan Lane III. A steady veteran like Reid could be just what they need to lock things down on the back end.

Los Angeles gets: S Justin Reid, 2027 fifth- and sixth-round picks (Nos. 144 and 181)

New Orleans gets: 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks (Nos. 128 and 163)

This deal is based off the Sydney Brown trade between the Philadelphia Eagles and Atlanta Falcons; New Orleans gets two better picks while offloading Reid's contract. Quentin Lake is holding it down in the box but Kamren Curl has struggled at free safety, and neither Kamren Kinchens nor Jaylen McCollough have held up well in coverage. The Rams are treading water at 4-4, and getting an upgrade without losing any picks (even if they're going to be picking later) has to be appealing after their big moves thus far.

#2719. Top 25 MLB trade candidates for 2026-27 offseason: Paul Skenes, Jeremy Peña and more who could move

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

With the Milwaukee Brewers crowned as the 2026 World Series champions, the 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is now upon us.

While the arc, pace, and even length of this offseason are all uncertain thanks to the ongoing CBA negotiations, we do know that at some point before the next season begins, we'll have a flurry of free agent signings and trades. The focus in this space right now is on the latter: possible winter trades.

We're about to examine the 25 leading trade candidates of the offseason. Obviously, this won't be an exhaustive list of players who might be traded, and just as obviously not all of these names to come will be on the move. Some, though, will, and all of these names have been deemed as distinct possibilities based on reporting, service time and payroll considerations, and prior organizational decision-making.

We'll explore names by putting them in groups based on the underlying reasons or causes of their status as trade candidates. Here are those groups:

The 25 names to come won't be ranked, but instead will be listed alphabetically within their respective categories. Now let's get to it.

Duran's taken a serious fall from the heights of 2024, when he earned an All-Star selection and cracked the top 10 of the American League MVP vote. He cratered last season, which makes this winter something of an inopportune time to trade him from the Boston standpoint. That said, the Red Sox have a crowded outfield with Wilyer Abreu, Ceddanne Rafaela, and Roman Anthony, which means a Duran swap may be needed to clear the decks. If nothing else, the 30-year-old outfielder presents a buy-low/change-of-scenery opportunity for a team looking to take a risk.

Potential fits: Phillies, Cubs, Mariners, Rangers

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 50%

Hernández has been a reliable power presence for the Dodgers, but now, at age 34, he's been showing some signs of decline. On another level, the Dodgers want to make space for elite prospect Josue De Paula to receive regular playing time, and there aren't any other paths to it. That may mean Hernández will be on the move.

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 45%

Kwan's another who's been a reliable presence in the trade rumors for some time. Cleveland also has a history of dealing core talents leading up to their walk year, and Kwan is indeed slated for free agency after next season. The timing would be right, as Kwan is coming off a 5.0-WAR season for the second time in his career.

Potential fits: Phillies, Blue Jays, Cubs, Mariners

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 30%

McClanahan's long and labored comeback from Tommy John surgery was finally realized this past season, and he turned in a strong age-29 campaign for the Rays. These, though, are the Rays, and McClanahan's forthcoming arbitration payday combined with his uncertain health history may prompt them to shop him to pitching-starved fellow contenders. He carries risk, of course, but there will no doubt be potential takers lining up for him.

Potential fits: Braves, Padres, Orioles, Tigers

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 35%

Thanks to a blazing fastball and wipeout knuckle curve, the soon-to-be 33-year-old Megill has been a lockdown closer for most of the last three seasons. The Brewers of course have a substantial history of trading away closers before they reach their high-salary years and also before they regress/decline (see: Hader, Josh and Williams, Devin). That could again be the case with Megill, who'll be in line for free agency after the 2027 season.

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 55%

He's the most dominant closer in baseball and the owner of one of the biggest fastballs ever, and he's under team control through the 2029 season. So why would the contending Padres trade Miller at the peak of his powers? They'd consider doing so because they have a lot of roster holes to fill elsewhere, especially with Michael King opting out of his contract. Trading away Miller would in theory allow them to fill some of those holes, which is why it'll be a temptation for lead executive AJ Preller. No doubt, fellow contenders will be lining up if the Pads do indeed shop the NL saves leader.

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 20%

Strider not so long ago was in the discussion for most dominant starter in the bigs, but persistent arm woes have turned him into a question mark. The Braves came close to dealing Strider at the deadline in exchange for more of a known quantity in the rotation, so there's basis for his inclusion on this list. Any team acquiring him will have to be comfortable with Strider's medicals and the fact that he's owed a minimum of $49 million over the next two seasons. His ace upside, though, is surely tantalizing.

Potential fits: Cardinals, Padres, Orioles, Tigers, Dodgers

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 25%

The Nats were clear sellers at the deadline, but they retained Abrams, who has two full years of team control remaining. In other words, it's going to take a lot to pry him away. At 26, he's coming off a 30-30 season, and he's been a quite productive bat over the last three years. Defensively, Abrams probably isn't an everyday shortstop moving forward, but second base is now in his toolkit.

Potential fits: Braves, Pirates, Red Sox, Giants, Rangers

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 25%

Teams will pay a lot for a young and controllable starting pitcher with frontline upside, and all of that describes the 27-year-old lefty Detmers. Not eligible for free agency until after the 2028 season, Detmers topped 4.0 WAR this past season and struck out 211 batters in 185 innings. For the Halos, trading him might be an example of selling high.

Potential fits: Cardinals, Red Sox, Cubs, Blue Jays, Padres

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 30%

As a 27-year-old All-Star catcher with three full seasons of team control remaining, Goodman would cost a lot in trade. Perhaps that's why the rebuilding Rockies will indeed deal him this winter. There's no doubt that playing his home games in Coors Field helps Goodman's cause, but this past season, he was actually much more productive on the road. Away from Coors, he hit 25 of his 41 home runs in 2026, and his road slugging percentage was .564 versus a .490 figure at a mile above sea level. That's power that will play anywhere.

Potential fits: Giants, White Sox, Yankees, Orioles

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 50%

Greene has one of the biggest fastballs in the game and a top 10 finish in the NL Cy Young balloting in his recent past. However, he's struggled to stay healthy and realize his potential on a sustained basis – the potential that made him the No. 2 overall draft pick in 2017. He's signed through 2028 with a club option for 2029, and it may be time for a change of scenery. He's been the subject of trade speculation before.

Potential fits: Dodgers, Braves, Red Sox, Astros, Blue Jays

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 25%

Herrera is not a particularly skilled defensive catcher outside of blocking pitches in the dirt, but he can get by behind the mask, at least on a part-time basis. He also has a plus bat, which will play at DH or perhaps first base and even left field. The Cardinals have an incoming glut of catchers, which means it may be time to move on from Herrera. He's not eligible for free agency until after the 2029 season.

Potential fits: Yankees, White Sox, Orioles, Giants

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 30%

The Marlins seem likely to trade away one of their middle infielders this winter, either the shortstop Lopez or second baseman Xavier Edwards. For now, we'll focus on Lopez, who would likely fetch the higher return. The 28-year-old Lopez this past season topped 6.0 WAR, led the NL in hits, and swiped 34 bases, all while grading out as a valuable defender at the premium position of short. He's under team control through the 2029 season, which means he'll have immense trade value.

Potential fits: Braves, Phillies, Red Sox, Rays

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 20%

The most underrated player in baseball? The 25-year-old Neto is very much in that discussion. Over the last three seasons, he's amassed a WAR of 15.6, which puts him in elite territory. Any team in need of excellence and stability on the left side of the infield should have interest. Neto isn't eligible for free agency until after the 2029 season, which adds to his already substantial trade value.

Potential fits: Braves, Red Sox, Tigers, Cardinals, Yankees

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 30%

No, this one isn't likely to happen, as Contreras has proved central to the Brewers' success in 2026 and for years prior. That said, the ever-resourceful Brewers do have a ready replacement on the roster in Bo Naylor. The 2026 World Series MVP is also in line for free agency after the 2027 season, which theoretically increases the chances that Milwaukee will explore his trade market. Speaking of which, such a skilled catcher with a potent bat and reputation as a leader will indeed have a healthy market.

Potential fits: Yankees, Rangers, Orioles

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 15%

For years now, it seems, we've been waiting for the Mariners to trade from their surfeit of starting pitching. They moved Luis Castillo at the deadline, but perhaps this time, they finally flip one of their big guns. Gilbert, 29, will be a pending free agent in 2027, which straightaway makes him a trade candidate for a Mariners club that's more averse to spending than they should be. He's an attractive one, too, as Gilbert has been a reliable source of innings over his career to date, and he also boasts a 3.58 FIP and a sparkling 5.14 K/BB ratio over the last four seasons.

Potential fits: Mets, Braves, Orioles, Cubs, White Sox

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 45%

Paredes, who turns 28 in February, is on a $13.35 million team option for 2027, and then he's eligible for free agency. That adds up to the real possibility of a trade out of Houston. While there are questions as to how Paredes' bat will play without the Crawford Boxes near at hand, there's no doubt he's overall a valuable performer. He's fresh off a 4.0-WAR season in 2026 and relatively young as notable trade targets go.

Potential fits: Phillies, Cardinals, Yankees

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 45%

Peña, like Paredes, will be a pending free agent in 2027, and the increasingly incompetent Astros may look to trade him as they did Kyle Tucker back in the winter of 2024-25. Peña, 29, hasn't been especially durable over the last two seasons, but when on the field, he remains an excellent all-around performer. If he is indeed shopped, then he's the most appealing shortstop on the trade and free agent markets this offseason.

Potential fits: Braves, Red Sox, Phillies

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 35%

Ryan has been the subject of trade speculation for what feels like the last half-decade. Has the time finally come for those rumors to be realized? Now 30, Ryan will be a free agent after the 2027 season, and that of course means he could be on the move this winter. He has excellent stuff, and over the last three seasons Ryan boasts an ERA+ of 117 and a K/BB ratio of 5.38.

Potential fits: Cubs, Astros, Mets, Orioles, Red Sox, Blue Jays

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 35%

Yes, deGrom is 38, but going into the final guaranteed year of his contract, he remains capable of being a solid rotation presence for a contender. deGrom reportedly used his full no-trade clause to block a trade to the Braves at the deadline, so it's far from certain whether he'd be willing to approve a deal out of Arlington. That said, such things are always negotiations, and a late-career run at the playoffs might prove tempting for him.

Potential fits: Braves, Dodgers, Blue Jays

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 25%

The future Hall of Famer is coming off another solid season once you consider that a spring hamate injury likely sapped his production early on. That said, he soon turns 33, and he's still owed $160 million through 2031. That's in addition to his full no-trade clause. The Mets and Lindor, though, may be at a crossroads in their relationship, which makes it at least theoretically possible that a change of scenery is in the offing.

Potential fits: Braves, Mariners, Phillies

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 15%

Marte already had a partial no-trade clause in his contract, which runs through 2030 (with a 2031 player option), and now he's earned a full no-trade clause through 10-and-5 rights. That said, after multiple somewhat bizarre AWOL incidents with the D-backs, Marte and the club may be looking for a fresh start. While Marte's offensive outputs dipped last season, his age-32 campaign, he still profiles as at least an above-average player for the near- to mid-term. And he may be more than that if he gets back to something like his pre-2026 peak.

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 30%

Now 32, Seager will always have health and durability concerns, but he remains a plus defensive shortstop who produces well at the plate by positional standards. With the Rangers perhaps looking to shed payroll, they could seek to move Seager, who's owed another $155 million through the 2031 season. As with the Mets and Lindor, that may mean kicking in cash to make a trade happen, but Seager would help the cause for any contender in need of help at the shortstop position.

Potential fits: Braves, Mariners, Phillies

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 20%

Will the increasingly listless Reds pivot toward a longer-term rebuild? If they do, then their electric 24-year-old shortstop could be dangled. De La Cruz is coming off his best season to date, and there's the feeling that he still has offensive upside in the tank. He's under team control through the 2029 season. Those three full years of control plus De La Cruz's MVP upside mean we'd be talking about a true blockbuster of a trade. No, it's not particularly likely to happen, but it's an intriguing possibility.

Chances he'll be traded (wild guess): 15%

This is becoming something of an annual exercise in speculation and wish-casting (wish-casting by non-Pirates fans, anyway). Skenes took a step back last season in terms of run prevention and underlying indicators, and he also lost a bit off his fastball. Still, he was overall a high-value pitcher who still projects as an ace, and he's not far removed from those legendary rookie and sophomore seasons. Like De La Cruz above, Skenes has three more full seasons before free agency, which makes his trade value pretty well stratospheric. The Pirates aren't likely at all to move him, particularly ahead of a new CBA that may benefit teams of their sort, but the Skenes trade conjecture isn't going anywhere.

Hunter Henry hasn't made progress in his injury recovery, presenting question marks for the New England Patriots ahead of their Week 9 matchup this weekend.

Henry has been playing in the NFL since 2016, going through his sixth season with the Patriots. He stands out as one of the better veteran tight ends in the league, helping New England make a deep playoff run to Super Bowl 60 last season.

However, Henry suffered a foot injury during the Patriots' win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 8. It has impacted him enough to the point that he has been absent from practices for two consecutive days, per reporter Mike Reiss.

"TE Hunter Henry, who was limited to eight snaps Sunday after injuring his foot, is absent from practice for the second day in a row," Reiss wrote on Thursday.

Henry has settled in as one of Drake Maye's top targets, having reached 85 targets, 60 catches and 650 yards each of the past two seasons. This year, he has caught 29 passes for 326 yards and two touchdowns in a balanced New England attack.

#2717. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

Jonathan Aranda belted a one-out solo homer off Gerrit Cole in the third inning and Rasmussen, who was making his second career postseason start and first since 2021, carried a no-hitter into the eighth. The Rays' right-hander retired the first two batters before Austin Wells ripped a double down the right-field line.

However, Wells made an ill-advised decision to attempt to stretch it into a triple and easily was thrown out at third. Closer Bryan Baker struck out two while retiring the Yankees in order in the ninth as Tampa Bay drew first blood.

New York attempts to avoid an 0-2 series deficit behind AL Cy Young Award favorite Cam Schlittler, who worked 6 2/3 scoreless innings in a victory over the Boston Red Sox in Game 1 of their Wild Card Series. The 25-year-old righty owns a 2.67 career ERA against the Rays but has won just one of his five starts. However, the Yankees are 3-2 in those contests, with two of the victories coming on the road.

Tampa Bay counters with Peralta, who is just 1-3 with a 4.32 ERA in nine career playoff appearances -- including six starts. The 30-year-old Dominican right-hander escaped with a no-decision in his only turn against the Yankees during the 2026 regular season as he gave up three runs on two hits and six walks over five innings on May 17 while with the New York Mets.

Don't look now, but Bob Chesney has UCLA ranked inside the top 25 just four games into his tenure. In fact, the Bruins are ranked even higher than that in Brandon Marcello's latest CFB Power Rankings.

UCLA had an open date last week as it geared up for a top-25 game against Oregon this weekend, but it still climbed into the top 10 of our rankings. Not only does Chesney have the Bruins offense humming, but he also has the chance to get a little revenge after leading James Madison against the Ducks in last year's College Football Playoff.

Here's a little snippet of the complete rankings:

21. Virginia Tech (-1) 22. Houston (NR) 23. Iowa (-7) 24. Mississippi State (-13) 25. USC (-2)

One team that's pretty far away from any top 10 ranking these days is Penn State, which is coming off a humiliating loss to Northwestern. The Nittany Lions plummeted 12 spots in the latest edition of the CBS Sports 138, and they're barely hanging on inside the top 50.

It won't be long before the 2026-27 NBA season tips off, and our team of experts is here to get you ready. Today, our own John Gonzalez is ranking the best starting fives from around the league.

In that regard, it's hard to beat the defending champion Knicks. Their quintet of oft-doubted stars returns after rolling to a title in last year's postseason. That said, they have serious competition within their own division.
